Subject: Competitive eval & model-quality next steps

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

1) Goals we heard from Acme:
- Improve answer fidelity for multi-step product-config flows (reduce hallucinations / incorrect attributes)
- Meet p95 latency <= 300ms for synchronous gen in the US region
- Keep inference unit costs below your current hyperscaler spend for high-volume paths

2) How Redwood proposes to help evaluate (short version):
- Run a focused quality + regression suite (we've attached a starter prompt set) that measures exact-match where applicable, hallucination rate, and a few downstream task metrics.
- Side-by-side throughput/latency pricing comparison vs Bedrock/text-bison and your current vendor.
- Test model variants: Redwood-Optimized Falcon-40B (quantized), OpenLLaMA v2-13B, and a tuned 8-bit variant — plus the hyperscaler endpoints you mentioned.

3) Immediate asks from us:
- Confirm the priority metric (hallucination reduction vs latency vs cost) and whether there are any golden records we should use for ground truth.
- Share a ~200-row sample of typical requests (anonymized) for calibration; if you prefer, upload to the Drive link below.
- Kickoff sandbox run: proposed 6/10 10:00 AM PT for a 30-min sync to align on scripts and dataset.

Attachments: acme-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (MAP), eval-prompt-set-v1.jsonl (starter prompts), redwood-eval-scripts.zip (runner + metrics snippets).

I've copied Neha and Aditya so we can spin up the sandbox and define the exact metrics. If the date/time doesn't work, propose alternatives and we'll adjust.

Subject: Re: Competitive eval & model-quality next steps (technical plan)

Marissa / Aditya — following up with a concise technical plan we can run in the sandbox. High level:

Evaluation scope:
- Quality: exact-match where applicable (config keys), F1 for attribute extraction, and a hallucination rate defined as: incidents where the model returns a value not present in the ground-truth reference or invents entities (measured as % of examples with at least one hallucinated field).
- Regression checks: run your existing golden set (if available) and compare model outputs across releases; compute delta in hallucination-rate and critical-miss rate.
- Safety/attribution: include prompt-injection probes for attribution/chain-of-thought leakage.

Metric thresholds (proposed):
- Hallucination rate target: <= 2.5% on the golden set (initial threshold for pass/fail).
- Latency: p95 <= 300ms for the synchronous path; p99 <= 600ms for bursty edges.
- Throughput baseline: 50 concurrent req/s sustained for the primary flow (we can scale this up if your traffic dictates).

Models & variants to test (parallel runs):
- Redwood-Optimized Falcon-40B (int8 quantized)
- OpenLLaMA v2-13B (tuned prompt template)
- Hyperscaler: AWS Bedrock (text-bison family)
- Hyperscaler: Google Vertex/PaLM2-family equivalent

Suggested test plan & artifacts:
1) Run eval-prompt-set-v1.jsonl (attached) against each model variant and collect metrics.
2) Run a regression suite on a 500-example golden subset (we recommend you provide or let us seed one).
3) Run hallucination-specific edge cases (we have ~40 probes in the scripts zip).

Deliverables from Redwood after the sandbox run:
- Per-model CSV with per-example outputs + per-field hallucination flags.
- A summary slide deck highlighting deltas vs hyperscalers (accuracy, hallucination, p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens).
- Recommendations: batching/quantization settings and a suggested rollout if you choose Redwood.

Links: runner + metric scripts (redwood-eval-scripts.zip attached), example runner notebook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1EvalSetExample

I'll provision a sandbox cluster in us-west-2 and spin up the three variants. Aditya — can you confirm we have the tuned Falcon snapshot and the 8-bit runner ready?

-Neha
